references.text: Moses says that the children of Israel grumble against the Lord, not just against him and Aaron. This shows that rebellion against God's chosen leaders is rebellion against God himself.
Aaron is defended against the people's complaints, and it is emphasized that the complaints are actually directed at the Lord.
Korah and his followers gather against Moses and Aaron, claiming that the entire congregation is holy. This is the background for the accusation of gathering against the Lord.
The Lord speaks about Israel's grumbling against him. The people's complaints against the leaders are counted as complaints against God.
The Lord speaks of the congregation that has conspired against him, using the same expression as in Korah's rebellion.
Samuel tells the people that they have not rejected him, but the Lord. To reject God's chosen servant is to reject God himself.
Jesus says that whoever rejects his messengers rejects him, and whoever rejects him rejects the one who sent him.
